intuition: A course is ready when none of its prerequisites remain unfinished. Put all ready courses in a queue. Taking one removes a requirement from its dependent courses, which may make them ready. If some courses never become ready, they are blocked by a cycle of requirements.

Treat prerequisites as directed edges from the prerequisite to its dependent. A course with zero incoming edges can be taken immediately. Removing it fulfills one requirement for each dependent; a dependent becomes ready only when every incoming requirement has disappeared. A queue separates courses ready now from courses still blocked.
If a disconnected component contains a cycle, other courses may finish normally but the completed count still exposes the unresolved component.

Every removed course has no prerequisites among the unremoved courses, so the removal order is legal. If all courses are removed, that order proves feasibility. Otherwise every remaining node has an incoming edge from another remaining node; repeatedly following predecessors in a finite graph reaches a cycle, which prevents completion.
Adjacency lists hold edges; indegrees and the ready queue hold courses.
The queue is iterative. A valid chain of 2000 courses has traversal depth 2000, but this reference stores pending courses explicitly rather than consuming a Python recursive call for every edge.

steps: Build edges 0→1, 0→2, 1→3, and 2→3. Initialize indegrees [0,1,1,2], ready=[0], and completed=0.
Pop course 0 and set completed=1. Its outgoing edges reduce indegrees of 1 and 2 to zero, so ready becomes [1,2].
Pop course 1 and set completed=2. Course 3 still has indegree 1: finishing only one of its two prerequisites cannot release it.
Pop course 2 and set completed=3. Decrement course 3 to zero and enqueue it.
Pop course 3 and set completed=4. All courses finished, so completed==numCourses and the result is true.

codeNotes.note: Correct edge direction lets completing a prerequisite notify its dependents rather than its ancestors.
A course enters the queue only after all requirements are satisfied, not merely after the first prerequisite finishes.
Courses left blocked imply a cycle; counting also includes isolated courses that had no prerequisites.

keyDecision: Enqueue a course only when its count of unfinished prerequisites becomes zero.

concept.question: How does removing finished prerequisites reveal the next ready courses?
intuition: Following prerequisites recursively can revisit the same requirements. The key question for each course is how many prerequisites are still unfinished.

Begin with courses that have no remaining requirements. Finishing one removes a requirement from each dependent course. A course becomes ready only when all its requirements have been removed. A directed cycle keeps its members waiting forever.
concept.observation: A dependent course becomes ready only when its remaining prerequisite count reaches zero.
approach: Count unfinished prerequisites for each course.
Take ready courses and remove their outgoing requirement obligations.
Return the completed order if requested, or whether all courses finish; a stalled incomplete process means a cycle.
concept.correctness: Each ready course has no unfinished prerequisites, so taking it respects all its constraints. Removing its requirements preserves the exact unfinished counts. If the process stalls with courses remaining, following an unfinished prerequisite backward in the finite remaining graph eventually repeats a node, exposing a cycle. Thus completion is equivalent to an acyclic feasible schedule.

complexity.explanation: Every course enters the ready queue once and every prerequisite edge is removed once. Work and graph storage are linear in courses plus requirements.

pitfalls: A dependent course becomes ready only when its remaining prerequisite count reaches zero.
Cycle members cannot release one another without an initial ready course.

scenes.title: Only course zero is initially ready
scenes.narration: Requirements are 0 before 1 and 2, then both 1 and 2 before 3. Initially only 0 has no unfinished prerequisites.
scenes.decision: Readiness means all requirements are finished, not merely one.

scenes.title: One prerequisite is still not enough
scenes.narration: Finishing 0 releases 1 and 2. Finishing 1 leaves course 3 still waiting for 2.
scenes.decision: Do not release a course after only one of several prerequisites.

scenes.title: The final requirement releases three
scenes.narration: Finishing 2 releases 3. All courses finish in order [0,1,2,3]. The answer is yes.
